arxiv-2110-13852.title: Optimal solutions to quantum annealing using two independent control functions
arxiv-2110-13852.creator: Marllos E. F. Fernandes, Emanuel F. de Lima, Leonardo K. Castelano
arxiv-2110-13852.description: Abstract We investigate the quantum computing paradigm consisted of obtaining a target state that encodes the solution of a certain computational task by evolving the system with a combination of the problem-Hamiltonian and the driving-Hamiltonian. We analyze this paradigm in the light of Optimal Control Theory considering each Hamiltonian modulated by an independent control function.

arxiv-2207-00954.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Shi-Liang Wu, Cui-Xia Li. To our knowledge, the error and perturbation bounds of the general absolute value equations are not discussed. In order to fill in this study gap, in this paper, by introducing a class of absolute value functions, we study the error and perturbation bounds of two types of the general absolute value equations (AVEs): A ​ x − B ​ | x | = b Ax-B|x|=b and A ​ x − | B ​ x | = b Ax-|Bx|=b .

arxiv-2211-07082.title: Learning Latent Part-Whole Hierarchies for Point Clouds
arxiv-2211-07082.creator: Xiang Gao, Wei Hu, and Renjie Liao
arxiv-2211-07082.description: Abstract Strong evidence suggests that humans perceive the 3D world by parsing visual scenes and objects into part-whole hierarchies. Although deep neural networks have the capability of learning powerful multi-level representations, they can not explicitly model part-whole hierarchies, which limits their expressiveness and interpretability in processing 3D vision data such as point clouds.

arxiv-2402-14026.title: Probability Tools for Sequential Random Projection
arxiv-2402-14026.creator: Yingru Li
arxiv-2402-14026.description: Abstract We introduce the first probabilistic framework tailored for sequential random projection, an approach rooted in the challenges of sequential decision-making under uncertainty. The analysis is complicated by the sequential dependence and high-dimensional nature of random variables, a byproduct of the adaptive mechanisms inherent in sequential decision processes.

arxiv-2404-08511.title: Leveraging Multi-AI Agents for Cross-Domain Knowledge Discovery
arxiv-2404-08511.creator: Shiva Aryal, Tuyen Do, Bisesh Heyojoo, Sandeep Chataut, Bichar Dip Shrestha Gurung, Venkataramana Gadhamshetty, Etienne Gnimpieba
arxiv-2404-08511.description: Abstract In the rapidly evolving field of artificial intelligence, the ability to harness and integrate knowledge across various domains stands as a paramount challenge and opportunity. This study introduces a novel approach to cross-domain knowledge discovery through the deployment of multi-AI agents, each specialized in distinct knowledge domains.

arxiv-2410-02389.title: Diffusion Meets Options: Hierarchical Generative Skill Composition for Temporally-Extended Tasks
arxiv-2410-02389.creator: Zeyu Feng, Hao Luan, Kevin Yuchen Ma, Harold Soh
arxiv-2410-02389.description: Abstract Safe and successful deployment of robots requires not only the ability to generate complex plans but also the capacity to frequently replan and correct execution errors. This paper addresses the challenge of long-horizon trajectory planning under temporally extended objectives in a receding horizon manner.

arxiv-2512-10309.title: Tracking large chemical reaction networks and rare events by neural networks
arxiv-2512-10309.creator: Jiayu Weng, Xinyi Zhu, Jing Liu, Linyuan Lü, Pan Zhang, Ying Tang
arxiv-2512-10309.description: Abstract Chemical reaction networks are widely used to model stochastic dynamics in chemical kinetics, systems biology and epidemiology. Solving the chemical master equation that governs these systems poses a significant challenge due to the large state space exponentially growing with system sizes.

pmc-10862238.creator: Linda Schönborn, Olga Esteban, Jan Wesche, Paulina Dobosz, Marta Broto, Sara Rovira Puig, Jessica Fuhrmann, Raquel Torres, Josep Serra, Roser Llevadot, Marta Palicio, Jing Jing Wang, Tom Paul Gordon, Edelgard Lindhoff-Last, Till Hoffmann, Lorenzo Alberio, Florian Langer, Christian Boehme, Eugenia Bi
pmc-10862238.description: Key Points•Highly prothrombotic, platelet activating PF4-dependent anti-PF4 antibodies can occur without preceding heparin or vaccination.•These antibodies are detectable in some sera obtained before the COVID-19 pandemic and the vaccination program. Introduction Antibodies directed against the chemokine platelet factor 4 (PF4) cause some of the most prothrombotic disorders in clinical medicine.

pmc-11491808.title: The effect of temperature and breathing pattern on the surface activity of ground squirrel pulmonary surfactant
pmc-11491808.creator: Akash Tejura, Mengxi Sun, Lynda McCaig, James Staples, Ruud Veldhuizen
pmc-11491808.description: This study investigates how hibernation affects the surface activity of pulmonary surfactant with respect to temperature and breathing pattern. Surfactant was isolated from a hibernating species, the 13-lined ground squirrel, and a homeotherm, the rabbit, and analysed for biophysical properties on a constrained sessile drop surfactometer.

pmc-11616238.title: Awareness, attendance, and attitudes toward cervical cancer screening among HIV-positive Chinese women in Yunnan province: a cross-sectional study
pmc-11616238.creator: Jiawei Hu, Rufei Duan, Hongyun Zhang, Xuelian Zhao, Aihui Wu, Le Li, Fanghui Zhao, Yong Zhang
pmc-11616238.description: BackgroundCervical cancer is a major health threat in the female population. Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV)-positive women encounter a higher risk of cervical cancer. It is significant to promote cervical cancer screening attendance among HIV-positive women. Little is known about the awareness, attendance, and attitudes toward cervical cancer screening, as well as the associated factors, among Chinese HIV-positive women.

pmc-11726847.title: Child Well-Being, Family Functioning, and Contextual Strain: A Study of Multi-Assisted Low-Income Families
pmc-11726847.creator: Paula Cristina Martins, Vítor Hugo Oliveira
pmc-11726847.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Objectives: This study aimed to examine the effects of poverty on child well-being and family functioning among low-income families. Specifically, it explored the role of parental stress, family dynamics, and contextual strain on children’s behavioral and emotional outcomes. Using a sample of families receiving welfare support, the research sought to assess the impact of conditional cash transfer programs and the involvement of Child Protective Services on child development and family well-being.

pmc-12598348.title: Evaluating the cross-reactivity of a stool methylated syndecan-2 (meSDC2) test in colorectal cancer detection
pmc-12598348.creator: Seung Wook Hong, Tae Jeong Oh, Sung Wook Hwang, Sang Hyoung Park, Byong Duk Ye, Jeong-Sik Byeon, Seung-Jae Myung, Suk-Kyun Yang, Sungwhan An, Dong-Hoon Yang
pmc-12598348.description: BackgroundA stool methylated syndecan-2 (meSDC2) test has demonstrated high sensitivity and specificity in diagnosing colorectal cancer (CRC). We aimed to evaluate the cross-reactivity of the meSDC2 test through multi-cancer analysis.MethodsThis study is a prospective, single-centre study. We recruited patients with 13 different types of cancers, including CRC, as positive control. Excluding those with CRC, participants did not undergo colonoscopy.

pmc-12815300.title: Pulmonary rehabilitation improves distance-saturation product in IPF: Greater benefits in patients with exercise-induced desaturation
pmc-12815300.creator: Hulya Sahin, Ilknur Naz, Fatma Demirci Uçsular, Gulistan Karadeniz
pmc-12815300.description: Background and aim:Exercise-induced dyspnea and desaturation are hallmark features of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) and are linked to disease severity and poor outcomes. The distance-saturation product (DSP), calculated by multiplying the walking distance by oxygen saturation, has been proposed as a mortality predictor.

pmc-13542225.title: Hypoadiponectinemia does not enhance anxiety-like behaviour in a lean PCOS-like mouse model
pmc-13542225.creator: Manisha Samad, Joakim Ek, Josefin Kataoka, Eva Lindgren, Claes Ohlsson, Ingrid Wernstedt Asterholm, Elisabet Stener-Victorin, Anna Benrick
pmc-13542225.description: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is characterized by reproductive and metabolic disturbances and associated with higher prevalence of anxiety and depression. Circulating adiponectin, an insulin-sensitizing adipokine, is reduced in women with PCOS, and low adiponectin has been linked to impaired mental health, particularly in females.

pmc-13592426.title: Inhibiting HuR-Mediated mRNA Stabilization Attenuates Psoriasis-Like Inflammation in Preclinical Models
pmc-13592426.creator: Dalila Paladino, Claudio G Atene, Martina Paganin, Elisabetta Palazzo, Marika Quadri, Alessandra Marconi, Dorian Tace, Lorenza Lazzari, Elena Trombetta, Michela Roccuzzo, Marta Tornese, Alessia Faiulo, Luca Reggiani Bonetti, Marco Manfredini, Gianluca Nazzaro, Angelo V Marzano, Daniela Arosio, Pierf
pmc-13592426.description: PurposePsoriasis is a chronic inflammatory skin disease characterized by hyperproliferative keratinocytes and activated Th17/Th1 lymphocytes, which sustain a self-perpetuating cycle by releasing pro-inflammatory cytokines. The RNA-binding protein (RBP) Human Antigen R (HuR) stabilizes many of these cytokine mRNAs, contributing to disease progression.

uslaw-usc-t26-s8004.title: 26 U.S.C. § 8004 — Appointment and compensation of staff
uslaw-usc-t26-s8004.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t26-s8004.description: United States Code, Title 26 (Internal Revenue Code); Chapter 91 (Organization And Membership Of The Joint Committee). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Except as otherwise provided by law, the Joint Committee shall have power to appoint and fix the compensation of the Chief of Staff of the Joint Committee and such experts and clerical, stenographic, and other assistants as it deems advisable.
